name: synthesize_O[C@H]1C2=CC3=CC=CC=C3O[C@H]2CCC1

input.prompt:
Propose a retrosynthesis route to synthesize the molecule with SMILES O[C@H]1C2=CC3=CC=CC=C3O[C@H]2CCC1. The route must have at least 2 reactions. The leaves on the retrosynthesis tree should be commercially available chemicals.

Here are some hints to help you (the hints are enumerated in the order that they should be applied): The Baylis-Hillman reaction is a carbon-carbon bond-forming reaction between an activated alkene (such as an acrylate or vinyl ketone) and an aldehyde or ketone, catalyzed by a nucleophilic catalyst (often a tertiary amine or phosphine). The reaction proceeds via the formation of a zwitterionic intermediate, which then undergoes nucleophilic attack on the carbonyl compound to form the desired product.

Ketones can be reduced to secondary alcohols using various reducing agents. Common reagents for this transformation include sodium borohydride (NaBH4) and lithium aluminum hydride (LiAlH4).
